security_spec.violation_condition: In XiangShan RTL, the LSU/LDU tag-check enable logic evaluates: tag_check_applies = (data_page.MTAG_bit_set && xIE_bit_clear) && (code_page.MTAG_bit_set && xIE_bit_set). This means load/store instructions fetched from a tagcheck-exempt code page (MTAG=1, X=1) trigger tag checks, while instructions fetched from normal code pages (MTAG=0) bypass tag checks — the exact inverse of the intended semantics where tagcheck-exempt code pages should always generate unchecked accesses per Rule 3 of the TAGGED_PAGE section.
security_spec.summary: Logic inversion in tag-check gating: RTL implementing the pre-fix spec would AND the tagged-data-page condition with 'instruction IS from tagcheck-exempt code page' instead of 'is NOT', systematically inverting which code regions trigger memory tag checks and effectively disabling tag protection for the majority of code.

findings.finding: PteBundle.perm sub-bundle lacks an mtag bit-field — only d,a,g,u,x,w,r,v are defined. Without this field, the PTW cannot extract the MTAG bit from page-table entries, making all downstream tag-check logic structurally impossible.
findings.snippet:
val perm = new Bundle {
  val d    = Bool()
  val a    = Bool()
  val g    = Bool()
  val u    = Bool()
  val x    = Bool()
  val w    = Bool()
  val r    = Bool()
  val v    = Bool()
}

findings.finding: isAf() only checks ppn_high overflow and v-bit. It does not detect the MTAG=1 && X=1 illegal combination which the spec requires to raise access-fault. A tagged executable page would silently pass isAf() and be treated as a valid leaf PTE.

isPf() checks reserved =/= 0.U as the first page-fault condition. If MTAG reuses a currently-reserved PTE bit, every PTE with MTAG=1 would falsely trigger a page-fault, making the feature unusable. Conversely, if MTAG does NOT overlap reserved bits, isPf() would not flag MTAG-related violations at all.

isGpf() has the same reserved-bit conflict as isPf(). For two-stage translation, a G-stage PTE with MTAG=1+X=1 would not be detected, and MTAG bits overlapping reserved bits would cause false guest-page-faults.

getPerm() propagates d,a,g,u,x,w,r from raw PTE to PtePermBundle but does not propagate mtag. The MTAG bit is silently dropped at the PTE→permission extraction boundary, so TLB fills carry zero MTAG information downstream.
findings.snippet:
pm.d := perm.d; pm.a := perm.a; pm.g := perm.g
pm.u := perm.u; pm.x := perm.x; pm.w := perm.w; pm.r := perm.r
pm

findings.finding: PtePermBundle — the cached permission representation in PtwEntry — has no mtag field. Every TLB hit on a tagged page returns zero MTAG information, making tag_check_enable always false regardless of PTE content.

TlbPermBundle.apply() propagates d,a,g,u,x,w,r from PtePermBundle but drops mtag. The TLB.perm_check() function — the central tag-check-enable decision point — receives a TlbPermBundle with no MTAG information to compute tag_check_enable = mtag && !x && mt_mode_enabled.
findings.snippet:
this.d := ptePerm.d; this.a := ptePerm.a; this.g := ptePerm.g
this.u := ptePerm.u; this.x := ptePerm.x; this.w := ptePerm.w; this.r := ptePerm.r

findings.finding: TlbResp — the TLB→LSU response bundle — has paddr, gpaddr, pbmt, miss, excp but no tagCheckEnable or mtag signal. The LSU load/store S2 stage has no way to know whether the current page requires tag checking. All pages look identical (normal/untagged), so tag checks are structurally impossible.

TLB.perm_check() — the central tag-check-enable decision point — handles R/W/X permissions, SUM, MXR, HLVX, pf/af/gpf enforcement, and A/D updates, but has zero MTAG logic. The computation tag_check_enable = perm.mtag && !perm.x && mt_mode_enabled is not implemented. There is no per-page signal telling LSU whether to compare pointer tags against memory tags.
findings.snippet:
val ldPermFail = !(modeCheck && Mux(hlvx, perm.x, perm.r || mxr(idx) && perm.x))
val stPermFail = !(modeCheck && perm.w)
val instrPermFail = !(modeCheck && perm.x)

findings.finding: EnvCfg CSR bundle — base class for menvcfg/senvcfg/henvcfg — has no MT_MODE field. Bits 34-60 are entirely absent. Without MT_MODE, tag checking can never be enabled via CSR configuration, so the tag_check_enable computation at TLB perm_check would always evaluate to false regardless of PTE.mtag.

LoadUnit S2 access-fault sources are: afUnaccessable, afVectorUncache, afUnalignMMIO, afTagError (DCache tag ECC, not MTE), afForwardDenied, afBypassDenied. No afMTagIllegal (MTAG=1+X=1) or afMTagMismatch (tag comparison failure) sources exist. Loads from tagged pages execute with no tag checking at all.
findings.snippet:
val afUnaccessable = uop.exceptionVec(loadAccessFault) || pmpUnaccessable
val afTagError = io.dcacheResp.bits.tag_error && tlbHit && io.csrCtrl.cache_error_enable
val af = afUnaccessable || afVectorUncache || afUnalignMMIO || afTagError || afForwardDenied || afBypassDenied

findings.finding: StoreUnit S2 access-fault sources are: afInaccessible, afVectorUncache, afCboUncache, afUnalignMMIO. No afMTagIllegal or afMTagMismatch sources exist. Stores to tagged pages execute without any tag validation.
findings.snippet:
val afInaccessible = uop.exceptionVec(storeAccessFault) || pmpInaccessible
val af = afInaccessible || afVectorUncache || afCboUncache || afUnalignMMIO

findings.finding: CSR-to-TLB signal routing propagates mPBMTE, hPBMTE, and PMM fields, but no MT_MODE or MTE-related enable signals. The TLB's perm_check() needs mt_mode_enabled as input to compute tag_check_enable; without this routing, the TLB cannot know whether the current privilege level has MTE enabled.
findings.snippet:
io.tlb.mPBMTE := RegNext(menvcfg.regOut.PBMTE.asBool)
io.tlb.hPBMTE := RegNext(henvcfg.regOut.PBMTE.asBool)
io.tlb.pmm.mseccfg := RegNext(mseccfg.regOut.PMM.asUInt)
